title: Slow Starters: Early-Season Patience and Buy-Low Targets
brief: Which players are likely to start the season slowly (rookies, players after long playoff runs, injury returns) and could be bought low in November trades? It must say how long to hold such players and which ones have early-season value instead.
summary: The best November buy-low targets are the three Knicks starters after their Finals run, plus top rookies like Cameron Boozer. Their managers will see weak early numbers that come from planned rest and rookie ramp-up, not lost talent. Hold these players through about the first 30 games or two months. Sell or drop the players whose early value depends on someone else's injury before that player returns.

paragraphs.text: Three groups tend to open the season below their level. The first is players from a long Finals run, who often show fatigue and lower production. Their teams also tend to rest them and trim starters' minutes early. The second is top rookies, who usually shoot poorly for about the first two months and then improve in the second half. The third is players coming back from injury, who return on minutes limits and ramp up slowly.

In our league this creates a trade window. Trades are frequent, and the deadline is 2027-03-04. Our playoffs run in weeks 19 to 21 and end on 2027-03-28. So a player who is weak in November but strong from January to March is worth more to us than his early stats show. The method note is plain: trade for the long term, buy low, sell high, and accept short-term pain for long-term gain.

The experts do not fully agree on how long the post-Finals dip lasts. One side says the slowdown lasts all year: players are exhausted the season after a title run, and the team is unlikely to repeat its production. The other side sees it as an early-season issue: teams rest players and trim minutes early, then let them play. The Knicks notes back the second view, with caution planned for about the first 30 games. In practice, buy these players at a discount in November, not at their draft price. A discount still pays off if the dip lasts all season, and it is a big win if it ends after 30 games.

sections.heading: Knicks after the Finals: the main November buys

paragraphs.text: Jalen Brunson, Karl-Anthony Towns and OG Anunoby all carry the same tag. The Knicks plan to be careful with starters' minutes and back-to-back rest for roughly the first 30 games after the Finals run. Expect lower minutes and some missed games in October and November. Managers who paid draft prices for them may get impatient. That is when to make an offer.

What to check before you offer: are their minutes per game creeping up, and are the rest days coming only on back-to-backs, not on single games? For Brunson, also check his wrist. For Towns, check whether his rebounds rise with Mitchell Robinson out. For Anunoby, check whether his steals hold up, since steals decide whether he lands near his best case. If minutes are rising and the role is intact, buy now. If minutes are flat after about 30 games, the season-long fatigue view is winning, so stop paying for a rebound.
Hold time if you own them: through about the first 30 games. Do not sell a Knicks starter in November for less than his full-season value. The weak start is expected and planned.

sections.heading: Rookies: hold for two months, buy before the ramp

paragraphs.text: Top rookies usually have poor efficiency for the first two months. If you drafted one, accept the slow start and do not drop him. Judge him only after about two months, which is around the end of the calendar year. Their second-half improvement lands right before our playoff weeks.

Cameron Boozer is the clearest case. He is projected outside the top 70 early but at a top-35 level in February and March, with a full 4-4-4 playoff schedule. He is a strong November buy from a manager tired of his early line. Check his minutes in Iisalo's short-stint rotation and his three-point attempts. The sites disagree on his threes, and that decides whether he helps your 3PM. Darryn Peterson should shoot badly and turn the ball over early, then improve. Hold him as a bench upside piece if he starts or gets real minutes next to George, Markkanen and Jackson Jr. Mikel Brown Jr. is likely bad until around February and has only 10 playoff games. He is a waiver watch, not a hold. Spend FAB only if he starts at point guard and the assists and steals show up.

Tyrese Haliburton is the top injury buy-low. Expect ramp-up and rust early, with play near his best from January to February. Check his minutes, how he handles back-to-backs, his efficiency and the ankle status. His playoff schedule is only 3-4-3, so value him on the regular season, not on weeks 19 to 21. Jalen Duren's minutes may sit at 27 to 28 early because of conditioning after his holdout. Buy him if his minutes climb above 28 and his usage grows with Tobias Harris gone. Fred VanVleet's minutes should rise during the season after his ACL return. He fits punt FG% builds, but check his knee, his minutes (about 30 expected), back-to-back rest and his weak 10-game playoff schedule.

Some returns are IL stashes, not buy-lows. We have 4 IL slots. Brandon Ingram is expected back around Thanksgiving to Christmas with minutes limits and rest. He has a good 4-3-4 Clippers playoff schedule. Jimmy Butler III is out until about Christmas to January. Check whether Golden State starts resting veterans before March 28. Yanic Konan Niederhäuser is out until about Christmas and is expected to start by February and March. Dereck Lively II is out until about Thanksgiving and then ramps up slowly behind Gafford and Johnson. Keep him on the waiver watch list rather than spending on him. For each of them, track the return date, then how long the minutes limit lasts. Hold through the ramp-up only if the return date holds.

Two late-season risers are worth noting. Gui Santos could reach top 70 after the trade deadline if Golden State rests veterans. Brayden Burries may get chances in March as Milwaukee moves toward its young players. Both are waiver checks after 2027-03-04, timed for our playoff weeks.

sections.heading: Early-season value: use it, then sell or drop

paragraphs.text: Some players are worth the most in October and November. Rostering them for the hot start and moving them at the right time is the other half of the buy-low plan. They are your trade chips for buying Knicks starters or rookies in November. Brandon Miller gets a high workload early while Coby White and Kon Knueppel are out. Check whether that extra usage drags his FG% and turnovers down. Tyler Herro's role may shrink as the Bucks shift minutes to young players during the season, and he may face trade talk before March 4. Plan to sell him while his numbers are strong.

Golden State and the Clippers have clear end dates. Brandin Podziemski handles the ball more while Butler is out. Yaxel Lendeborg's numbers should drop when Moody and Butler return. Sell or drop both before Butler comes back around Christmas to January. Isaiah Jackson starts while Konan Niederhäuser is out, so drop him when Konan Niederhäuser returns. Derrick Jones Jr. starts only while Ingram, Beal and other Clippers are out.

Al Horford and Kyle Kuzma are waiver streams only. Horford starts at center while Porzingis is out but sits every back-to-back, so use daily lineups to start him only on non-back-to-back days. Kuzma opens as a starter but could lose minutes by December or March. Pick him up only if he keeps the starting job and plays clearly more than 26 minutes. With a cap of 6 acquisitions per week, spend those moves on short-term starters and keep your slow starters on the roster.
